item.title: Xi urges police to uphold duty as guardians
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-16
Xi urges police to uphold duty as guardians He calls on officers nationwide to remain strongly dedicated to Party and people President Xi Jinping has called on the country's police officers to remain committed to serving the people, be loyal guardians of the Party and the people, and demonstrate a strong sense of responsibility and dedication. Xi, who is also general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, made the remarks in a reply letter to a primary-level police force in Zhangzhou, Fujian province. Recently, members of the "Zhangzhou 110" police unit wrote to Xi, reporting on their work and expressing their determination to fulfill duties on the new journey. In his reply letter, Xi lauded the unit's police officers for their dedication and hard work at the grassroots level in serving the public and maintaining social stability for the people. He emphasized that the police bear the important responsibility of safeguarding the people's well-being and the country's peace, calling on police officers nationwide to uphold fine traditions, devote themselves to wholeheartedly addressing the needs and concerns of the people, and work diligently to protect the safety of the public. In China, "Dial 110 in case of emergency" is a well-known phrase. The "Zhangzhou 110" unit is one of the exemplary primary-level units within China's police forces. Since 1990, it has pioneered and continuously improved a rapid response mechanism tied to the 110 police emergency call service, playing a significant role in combating crime, maintaining public security and serving the community. While working in Fujian in the 1990s, Xi visited the police unit three times to inspect and guide its work. During an inspection tour in 1996, Xi, who was then deputy secretary of the CPC Fujian Provincial Committee, emphasized that the work of the 110 police emergency call service is fundamental to serving the public, according to a report by the People's Daily Overseas Edition. The emergency call service is an important channel for the Party committee to connect with the people, and it also strengthens the bond between public security agencies and the people, Xi said at that time, praising the unit's police officers as "people's guardians". Previously, public security officers were considered to be mainly responsible for handling cases such as maintaining public order and combating crime. After the "Zhangzhou 110"police unit was established, citizens found they could also seek assistance from the police for such matters as helping elderly people who lose their way return home, or mediating neighborhood disputes. However, there were discussions in the unit about the duties of police. In one case, a local pregnant woman dialed 110 to ask the police to take her to the hospital, since her family members were away and she was about to deliver. Police officers helped her, but some complained that they worked like housekeepers instead of police. A lively debate led to a consensus: As people's police under the leadership of the Party, serving the public is an unshirkable duty. Consequently, the "Zhangzhou 110" police unit established a principle: "The people's difficulties are our difficulties, and the people's satisfaction is our greatest wish." Over the years, the "Zhangzhou 110" police unit has made many institutional innovations and reforms. It has also improved its speed in handling incidents with the help of modern technology. "Compared to fighting crime, it's more often that we offer assistance to ordinary people. When we respond one second earlier, that's one second sooner that the public can feel at ease," said Wang Shaohui, a police officer of the "Zhangzhou 110" unit. Wan Lin, another officer in the unit, said that upon reading the reply letter from Xi, he felt greatly inspired. "General Secretary Xi emphasized in the letter that the police bear the important responsibility of safeguarding the people's well-being and the country's peace. This has provided direction and injected strong motivation for us young police officers to fulfill our duties," Wan said. "I will respond to every call for help and resolve every dispute with care and dedication, ensuring peace and tranquility in our community," he added. Yang Jie in Fuzhou contributed to this story. Contact the writers at caodesheng@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: China-ASEAN trade receives protocol push
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-16
China-ASEAN trade receives protocol push Supply chain links deepen, cooperation extends to digital and green economies China and the member states of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations are becoming more closely intertwined through trade, supply chains and consumer markets, with their economic ties extending beyond traditional areas of cooperation, said market watchers and business leaders. That shift is gathering momentum as the China-ASEAN Free Trade Area 3.0 Upgrade Protocol, or CAFTA 3.0, and the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership, or RCEP, are expected to lower trade barriers and make it easier for companies to operate across regional markets. As the two sides seek to inject new impetus into regional and global economic growth, China is working with ASEAN members to bring the upgraded protocol into force at an early date, according to information released this month by the Ministry of Commerce. The 23rd China-ASEAN Expo, which is scheduled to be held in Nanning, Guangxi Zhuang autonomous region, from Thursday through Monday, will focus on opportunities arising from CAFTA 3.0 and promote cooperation in new areas including the digital economy, green development and supply chain connectivity. Xu Liping, director of the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences' Center for Southeast Asian Studies, said the China-ASEAN relationship is increasingly being shaped by the way production networks have spread across the region. Chinese companies are sourcing, manufacturing and selling more within Southeast Asia, while ASEAN businesses are gaining greater access to China's vast consumer and industrial markets, Xu said. Lin Honghong, vice-chairperson of the China Council for the Promotion of International Trade, noted that CAFTA 3.0 is extending business cooperation beyond traditional trade and investment to new areas such as the digital and green economies. The agreement is also promoting closer links between industrial and supply chains across the region, creating more opportunities for companies on both sides, she said. CAFTA 3.0, which was signed in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, in October 2025, marks the latest stage in the evolution of the China-ASEAN Free Trade Area. CAFTA was launched in 2002 and fully implemented in 2010. The upgraded CAFTA 2.0 protocol was signed in 2015, and it took full effect in 2019. Data from the General Administration of Customs shows that the value of China-ASEAN trade reached 5.95 trillion yuan ($886 billion) in the first eight months of 2026, up 20.6 percent year-on-year. Ruijie Networks Co, a manufacturer of switches, routers and network security equipment for data centers based in Fuzhou, Fujian province, saw its exports to ASEAN markets surge 93 percent year-on-year to reach 1.44 billion yuan between January and August. Wang Chenyan, director of external relations at Fujian Star-net Communication Co, the parent company of Ruijie Networks, said that demand for networking equipment has grown rapidly in Southeast Asia, particularly in Singapore, Malaysia and Indonesia, amid rising investment in digital infrastructure and data centers. According to Fuzhou Customs, the value of Fujian-ASEAN trade reached 159.14 billion yuan in the first seven months of this year, up 4.9 percent year-on-year. Futaihua Precision Industry (Weihai) Co, a manufacturer of printers and related equipment based in Weihai, Shandong province, imported over 300 million yuan worth of industrial components from Southeast Asian countries, including Cambodia and Malaysia, during the January-August period, a year-on-year increase of 320 percent. Statistics from Qingdao Customs show that during the first seven months of this year, ASEAN was Shandong's largest source of imports, with shipments valued at 196.66 billion yuan, up 9.5 percent year-on-year, accounting for 22.8 percent of the province's total imports.

item.title: Cooperation key to common prosperity
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-16
Cooperation key to common prosperity Officials, experts and grassroots representatives on Tuesday called for stronger coordination in regional development, continued efforts to safeguard and improve people's well-being through development, and solid progress toward common prosperity. They made the remarks at a seminar on the theory and practice of Fujian-Ningxia cooperation in Yinchuan, capital of the Ningxia Hui autonomous region. Li Shulei, a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and head of the Publicity Department of the CPC Central Committee, attended and addressed the seminar. In 1996, China launched the program of East-West Pairing-off Cooperation for Poverty Reduction under which a developed provincial region in the east assisted a less-developed region in the west. While serving as a provincial leader in East China's Fujian province in the late 1990s, President Xi Jinping personally oversaw the progress of pairing-off cooperation between Fujian and Ningxia, opening up a successful path and creating a model for cooperation between China's eastern and western regions. Participants at the seminar said that since the 18th CPC National Congress in 2012, the CPC Central Committee has placed east-west cooperation in an important position in national governance, made a series of strategic plans and advanced innovative practices, leading to historic achievements in such cooperation in the new era. They underlined the importance of adhering to a people-centered approach to development, and efforts to make full use of China's political and institutional strengths. Participants called for the development of cultural undertakings and industries in accordance with local conditions to enrich people's cultural lives, while strengthening the protection of historical and cultural heritage and harnessing culture to support the economic and social development of western regions. Theoretical research and news coverage should be strengthened, they said, calling for efforts to summarize the valuable experience of Fujian-Ningxia cooperation and tell compelling stories of east-west cooperation in the new era.

item.title: High-tech sector lifts industrial growth
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-16
High-tech sector lifts industrial growth China's economy drew strong support from new growth drivers in August, with double-digit growth in high-tech manufacturing and solid external demand underpinning fast industrial growth, officials and experts said on Tuesday. However, the transition from old to new growth drivers remains marked by structural divergence, they cautioned, adding that a more proactive policy response is needed to revive domestic demand after a second straight month of slower retail sales growth and a deepening contraction in fixed-asset investment. Their remarks came on the heels of fresh data released by the National Bureau of Statistics on Tuesday showing that the country's industrial output rose 5.2 percent year-on-year in August, accelerating from a 4.5 percent increase in July. According to Fu Linghui, the bureau's spokesman and chief economist, the strong performance was underpinned mainly by new growth drivers, which accounted for over 60 percent of industrial output growth. High-tech and digital product manufacturing, for example, grew 16.7 percent and 15.7 percent year-on-year, respectively. "The bright spot remains industrial activity," said Lynn Song, chief economist for China at Dutch bank ING, pointing to resilient external demand and China's continued technological and industrial upgrading. That upgrading is taking China beyond its traditional strengths in low-cost, large-scale manufacturing toward "ecosystem and innovation leadership", US investment bank Morgan Stanley said in a recent report. The report projected that the transition could raise the country's potential GDP level by about 3.5 percent by 2035 and lift its share of global manufacturing value-add from around 28 percent to 30 percent. The growing role of new growth drivers was also evident in investment, with spending in high-tech industries rising 5.2 percent year-on-year in the first eight months. "The investment mix in manufacturing is improving," said Wang Qing, chief macroeconomic analyst at Orient Golden Credit Rating International. Also, the services sector is shifting toward more technology-intensive activities, with information transmission, software and information technology services contributing more than one-fifth of overall growth in services production in August, the NBS said. In contrast to the strong performance of emerging sectors, weak domestic demand continued to weigh on the broader economy, with consumption growth moderating and the contraction in investment deepening, analysts said. Retail sales, a key gauge of consumption, rose 0.4 percent year-on-year in August, slowing from 0.6 percent in July, while fixed-asset investment fell 7.2 percent year-on-year in the first eight months, compared with a 6.7 percent decline in the January-July period, the NBS said. "New growth drivers have yet to fully offset the weakening of traditional ones," said Luo Zhiheng, chief economist and head of the research institute at Yuekai Securities, calling for quicker issuance of special-purpose bonds and accelerated fiscal spending. Experts said ample policy room is still available, additional measures — including interest rate and reserve requirement ratio cuts, and further issuance of government bonds — are expected to help strengthen growth momentum toward the year-end. Wen Bin, chief economist at China Minsheng Bank, said policy support is strengthening and implementation is accelerating, noting the recent recapitalization plans totaling up to 360 billion yuan ($53.6 billion) for State-owned financial institutions. New policy-based financial instruments totaling 800 billion yuan began rolling out in early September, with funding expected to be deployed mainly in September and October, Wen added. Echoing that view, Sheana Yue, a senior economist at British think tank Oxford Economics, said: "Accelerated bond issuance and policy-bank financing are likely to eventually boost government investment." On the monetary front, Wang of Orient Golden Credit Rating International said the central bank could cut interest rates by 10 basis points and the reserve requirement ratio by 0.5 percentage point around the end of the third quarter. Such easing would help boost consumption, stabilize investment and support the property market, he said.

item.title: HK CE unveils first-ever five-year plan
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-16
HK CE unveils first-ever five-year plan Share - WeChat
Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Chief Executive John Lee Ka-chiu started delivering the SAR's first-ever five-year plan on Wednesday morning. The strategic roadmap, which aims to align with the nation's 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-30), will map out Hong Kong's development direction for a five-year term, covering areas such as the development of the Northern Metropolis, economy, innovation and technology, medical and social welfare. After introducing the core of the five-year plan, Lee will continue to deliver the 2026 Policy Address, also the current administration's final annual policy blueprint. Lee is expected to finish delivering the two documents in about three hours.

item.title: Good chicken keeps its flavor with just a peck of seasoning
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-16
"No chicken, no feast." The saying still holds true in Guangdong province, where poultry remains a fixture on family tables and banquet menus, while some local specialties are finding new fans beyond the dining table. At LN Dongfang Hotel in Guangzhou, the provincial capital, Shishi chicken has been prepared for 65 years. From Fengkai county in western Guangdong, Xinghua chickens are shipped across China, with their eggs also sought by pastry chefs. Yet as the way that chicken is produced, served and consumed changes, one standard remains: The chicken itself should taste like chicken. "That is the highest praise Guangzhou diners can give," said Lu Jianrong, executive chef at Yanlegong, a restaurant at the hotel. The aim is chicken that is tender yet firm, with a fresh, savory flavor that is not masked by seasoning, Lu said. This emphasis on natural flavor has shaped Guangdong's rich tradition of chicken dishes and local breeds. One example is Shishi chicken, a traditional Guangzhou dish created in the early 20th century at Xinji, a Cantonese restaurant on what is now Beijing Road. It was named after the nearby Guangzhou Municipal Normal School, known as "Shishi". For Lu, it starts with the bird itself. The restaurant uses chickens aged 160 to 180 days. "Only a chicken that has been raised for long enough can develop the right flavor," Lu said. The key cooking method is slow-poaching rather than plain boiling. The chicken is cooked in stock, kept at about 85 C, that is made with ingredients including ham, shrimp, dried scallops, squid, ginger and scallions. A technique known as "three lifts and three dips" helps to regulate the temperature and cook the chicken evenly. "If the water is too hot, the skin can split and the meat can become tough; if it is too cool, the chicken may not cook properly," Lu said. Knowing when it is done also takes experience. Chefs feel the leg joint to judge doneness, rather than relying solely on a timer. "Machines can measure temperature, but every chicken is different in size and texture," Lu said. "The final judgment still requires a chef to make adjustments based on the individual bird." Once cooked, the chicken is quickly cooled in chilled stock, then cut into pieces and finished with roasted peanut oil and a savory soy-based sauce. "The sauce is there to enhance the chicken's flavor, not to cover it up," Lu said. The same preference for freshness and natural flavor can be found in Guangdong's local breeds. Xinghua chicken, from Fengkai county, is a national geographical indication product known for its small size, thin skin and tender meat. Locals describe it as having "glass-like skin and crisp, delicate bones". Chen Yanying, who runs a restaurant specializing in dishes made with Xinghua chicken, said the restaurant works with local farms to maintain a steady supply. The breed is also finding new uses beyond the dining table. Its eggs are being made into cakes, pastries and egg pancakes, while the restaurant's partner farms sell about 2 million birds a year, with the majority shipped beyond Guangdong. Poached Xinghua chicken is among the most popular preparations. The chicken is repeatedly lifted from hot water, briefly cooled and returned to the pot. The method produces crisp skin and tender meat, with a gelatinous layer forming between the skin and flesh. In Fengkai, it is commonly served with ginger-and-scallion soy sauce, while Guangzhou diners often pair it with minced ginger and peanut oil. For visitors to Guangdong, especially those trying Cantonese cuisine for the first time, local chicken offers a straightforward introduction to the region's culinary philosophy — start with the ingredient and let the cooking reveal its natural qualities. Though the preparations differ, the principle is the same: Seasoning should complement the ingredient rather than overwhelm it. "Cantonese cuisine emphasizes freshness, lightness, crispness, tenderness and smoothness," Lu said. "With good ingredients, you don't need too many complicated seasonings. The key is to bring out their natural flavor." Zheng Caixiong in Guangzhou contributed to this story.

item.title: Heilongjiang leverages black soil culture
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-16
Heilongjiang leverages black soil culture Fertile paddies in NE China, customized experience making rice a true cash crop As the country's "granary", Northeast China's Heilongjiang province has continuously produced high-quality grains, laying a solid foundation for national food security. In recent years, the province has actively explored new paths for agricultural transformation and upgrading as consumers begin to place greater importance on food traceability, production involvement and rural cultural experiences. The province is vigorously developing customized agricultural models such as paddy field adoption and exclusive order-based planting, shifting consumer demand to the forefront of field production and giving end-users a more personal, hands-on experience with the staple grain. By integrating immersive cultural and tourism scenarios like paddy field sightseeing, agricultural study tours and intangible cultural heritage harvest festivals, the strategy marks a shift in the rice cultivation sector from merely selling products to selling experiences and culture. In Wuchang, Harbin, through its rice field adoption and custom farming programs, Qiaofu Dayuan Agricultural Co Ltd draws on the city's intangible cultural heritage of agricultural festivals, creating an immersive rice farming study system, said Wang Dan, administrative manager of the company. The company manages 250,000 mu (16,667 hectares) of rice fields at the core production area of Wuchang rice, which is famous for its unique flavor and texture, and is grown in traditional Northeast China black soil known for its highly fertile characteristics. The company has innovatively introduced a personalized model based on square meters, launching an annual family package for 100-sq m rice paddies, offering services including freshly milled rice delivery and farming experiences, Wang said. In 2026, the company achieved high-end rice field adoption of 3,333 hectares, with contracted sales of 195 million yuan ($29 million), and group client customization of 8,666 hectares, with contracted sales of 890 million yuan. Through standardized planting, diversified customization and full-chain services, the company continues to enhance the golden brand of customized agriculture centered on Wuchang rice. Lots of adoption clients have visited their adopted rice fields to participate in festival activities and experience the joys and challenges of harvesting. The park is equipped with a rice culture museum, sightseeing trails, specialty homestays and rice field photo spots, transforming rice production into a new agricultural, cultural and tourism business model integrating sightseeing, study, experience, aesthetics and consumption. For 11 consecutive years, the company has held agricultural festivals such as the Rice Planting Festival, Rice Flower Festival and Rice Harvest Festival. In 2024, the company established the Rice Countryside Town Study Base, creating a comprehensive study project integrating rice science popularization, farming practices and cultural experiences. The study courses cover visits to the rice culture museum, rice growth science education, hands-on farming experiences like planting and harvesting, rice processing observation and understanding the rice-duck symbiosis ecosystem. Visitors can enter the fields to experience farming and harvesting, to understand "every grain comes from hard work", while learning about the historical origins of Wuchang rice and the mystique of black soil farming culture.

item.title: Fahai Temple murals: 'Naked-eye 3D' from 500 years ago
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-16
Mural painting is where painting began. Chinese murals, with their long and distinguished tradition, unfold like a history of painting written across walls. Alina Efimova, a cultural observer from Russia with a deep interest in Chinese murals, sat down with Dong Zhuo, vice dean of the School of Restoration at the Central Academy of Fine Arts, for a cross-cultural conversation. Amid the vast and dazzling array of Chinese murals, what makes the murals of Fahai Temple so exceptionally refined? Why do netizens describe them as having a "naked-eye 3D" quality? And where does that faint halo of light come from? Follow their conversation to take in the grandeur and exquisite beauty of the Fahai Temple murals — a masterpiece of imperial mural painting from the Ming Dynasty (1368-1644). Into Chinese Art is an immersive cultural interview series produced by China Daily Culture Channel, where international hosts engage with art experts through interactive discussions, offering audiences a deeper understanding of Chinese art and aesthetics. The fourth season of Into Chinese Art focuses on murals.

item.title: Pinglu Canal opens, connecting Southwest China to the sea
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-16
Pinglu Canal opens, connecting Southwest China to the sea The Pinglu Canal, a major waterway linking inland areas of Southwest China with the sea, officially opened to navigation on Wednesday in South China's Guangxi Zhuang autonomous region. Spanning 134.2 kilometers, the canal connects the Xijiang River system, a significant inland shipping artery in southern China, with the Beibu Gulf, providing inland areas of Southwest China with more direct access to the sea. This canal is China's first nationally planned canal since 1949, designed to grant inland waterways direct access to the sea. Construction began on Aug 28, 2022, with a total investment of approximately 72.7 billion yuan ($10.83 billion). The canal is designed to accommodate vessels of up to 5,000 metric tons. As a key component of the New International Land-Sea Trade Corridor, the canal offers a shorter water route from parts of Southwest China to the coast. For some cargo, it will reduce the inland shipping distance to the sea by more than 560 kilometers. The new route also provides western China with more direct access to ports on the Beibu Gulf, strengthening transport links between inland areas and overseas markets.

item.title: Trust, dialogue highlighted at forum
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-16
Trust, dialogue highlighted at forum Experts and officials called for greater trust, dialogue and cooperation amid growing uncertainties in the international environment at the 13th Beijing Xiangshan Forum in Beijing on Tuesday. Speaking at parallel sessions of the forum, experts from various countries said that the international landscape is experiencing profound changes and multilateral institutions need to adapt in order to remain relevant and effective in addressing emerging challenges. Carlos Branco, former director of cooperation and regional security at NATO International Military Staff, said the evolution of the United Nations system has been marked by insufficient mutual trust and goodwill. He pointed to several "loopholes" in the current international system, including unilateral sanctions and tariffs, as well as the use of force outside the framework of international law. Francisco Cafiero, director of Argentina's Manuel Ugarte Institute of International Affairs and Political Studies, said that the international community needs greater trust and dialogue amid rising uncertainties. Branco said that the Global Governance Initiative proposed by China provides a new perspective on addressing these problems, highlighting principles that are also fundamental to the UN Charter — the rule of international law, multilateralism and respect for sovereignty. "This is what the world needs," Branco said. If humanity wants to move forward, rather than fall into global confrontation, and avoid conflicts between major powers, countries need to adhere to these basic principles, he added. He said that the initiative reflects China's desire to uphold the post-World War II international order, rather than establish a new one. Cafiero said the initiative aims to provide greater certainty to the world. Regarding growing inequality around the world, he highlighted China's experience in eliminating extreme poverty in 2020, saying that countries of the Global South could learn from China's practices and work together toward the goal of eradicating extreme poverty. The Beijing Xiangshan Forum, which runs from Tuesday to Thursday, has brought together nearly 100 official delegations from countries, regions and international organizations. This year's forum is themed "Build Consensus on Stability, Advance Security Governance Together". Yusne bin Hj Mokhtar, chief executive of the Malaysian Institute of Defence and Security, called on multilateral institutions to adapt to the evolving international environment in order to remain relevant, responsive and effective in addressing new challenges. He said that effective multilateralism should be inclusive, rules-based and grounded in international law, while respecting the sovereignty and strategic choices of every country. "The real value of multilateralism is demonstrated not when we agree on everything, but when countries with different perspectives are still able to manage differences peacefully and cooperate where they are converged," Yusne said. Equality emphasized Yukio Hatoyama, former Japanese prime minister and president of the East Asian Community Institute, said equality among countries in the international community should be ensured to realize multilateralism. "Countries should act according to rules rather than strength, and we must also ensure that all countries have a role in the process," he said. Experts at the forum also called for new international rules and frameworks to govern emerging fields, particularly artificial intelligence. Hatoyama said that against the backdrop of the growing use of AI in military operations, "we are witnessing a form of warfare in which the attacker may not even see the blood or the faces of those who are suffering". He emphasized that the international community needs to establish new regulatory frameworks for emerging technologies and that international treaties should take into account the use of AI.
